generic.title: Before you use this calculator
paragraphs: This calculator provides an indicative estimate of your pay entitlement for the hours entered. Do not use it to make payroll decisions or to process or approve employee payments. It does not provide legal, industrial relations, payroll, taxation or accounting advice. Do not rely on it to determine an employee’s legal entitlement or an employer’s payroll obligation.

Results depend on the information entered and the rules configured in the calculator. Payment decisions must be based on the applicable industrial instrument, employment contract, roster and payroll records. Seek payroll, legal or industrial relations advice where required.
For accurate workplace pay and entitlement information, please contact the Fair Work Ombudsman or visit fairwork.gov.au.

Testing access only: named accounts use a shared password and are intended only for controlled testing. Full user authentication is not yet live. Do not use these accounts for sensitive or production data.

fast_food.title: Scope and assumptions
paragraphs: This calculator provides a guide to selected payments for adult employees under the Fast Food Industry Award 2020. It applies the configured ordinary-hour limits, casual loading, minimum paid engagements for part-time and casual employees, weekday late-night and early-morning penalties, weekend and public-holiday rates, daily and period overtime thresholds, and two-tier Monday-to-Saturday overtime rates.
assumptions: The selected instrument, classification, employment type, base hourly rate and entered shift details are correct, and the employee is covered by the Fast Food Industry Award 2020 without an enterprise agreement or other overriding arrangement.

All calculations are based on one two-week pay period. The calculator assesses full-time ordinary hours against 76 hours for the pay period. Part-time and casual period thresholds are assessed weekly.

For part-time employees, the contracted-hours entry must match the employee’s current agreed ordinary hours per week. The calculator uses this value as the weekly overtime threshold. If no value is entered, it uses 38 hours per week.
Entered start and finish times, unpaid breaks, public-holiday selections and any manual ordinary-time or overtime selections accurately reflect the employee’s records and applicable arrangements.
Any manual ordinary-time or overtime selection applies to the whole entered shift. The user must ensure that the selected classification is appropriate.
limitations: The calculator approximates the Award’s five-days-per-week rule by applying a maximum of 10 worked days across the two-week pay period. This includes the exception that permits 6 days in one week when no more than 4 days are worked in the following week.

The calculator supports roster-based overtime through manual classification. The user must manually classify any hours worked outside a full-time employee’s roster. For a part-time employee, the user must manually classify hours worked outside the days, start and finish times, or meal-break arrangements in the employee’s agreed or validly varied regular pattern.
Sunday ordinary-hour penalties default to the Level 1 rate. The higher Sunday ordinary-hour rates for Level 2 and Level 3 employees are not selected automatically.

For day workers, the calculator deducts the unpaid break duration entered for each shift. Default day-worker shifts start with a 30-minute unpaid break; shiftworker shifts start with no break deduction. Break entitlements and compliance must be checked separately against the roster and Award.

The user selects public holidays and manual classifications and must confirm the applicable date, location and substitution arrangements. If only part of a shift requires manual classification, the user must enter that part as a separate shift segment.
exclusion_intro: The calculator only applies the configured rules shown under ‘Show ruleset’ and described above.
Specific areas which are not covered include:
exclusions: The 4-hour minimum payment for Sunday overtime that is not continuous with ordinary hours.
Junior, apprentice, trainee, supported-wage and school-based trainee rates.
Classification progression, higher duties, future annual wage changes and minimum-wage compliance.
Allowances and reimbursements, including meals, uniforms, cold work, travel, vehicle use and other expenses.
Split or broken shifts, recalls, call-backs, time off instead of overtime, and minimum-payment rules other than the configured part-time and casual minimum engagements.
Leave, leave loading, superannuation, tax, deductions, termination payments, interest and back-pay calculations.
Enterprise agreements, annualised salaries, individual flexibility arrangements, employment-contract terms and other arrangements that may apply instead of or alongside the Award.
closing_paragraphs: These assumptions, limitations and exclusions must be checked against the employee’s actual employment arrangements, roster and payroll records.

woolies_2024_demo.title: Scope and assumptions
paragraphs: This calculator provides a guide to selected payments for adult employees under the Woolworths Australian Food Group Agreement 2024. It calculates ordinary pay, casual loading, minimum paid engagements, weekday and weekend penalties, public-holiday rates, overtime, shiftwork rates and insufficient-break payments.
assumptions: The employee is a wages-paid team member covered by the Woolworths Australian Food Group Agreement 2024, and the selected classification, employment type and worker type are correct.

The hourly rate entered is the correct adult non-casual base rate for the employee’s classification. For casual employees, the calculator applies both the casual loading and any applicable penalty or overtime rate.
All calculations are based on one two-week pay period.

The calculator applies an insufficient-break payment when the employee has fewer than 10 hours between shifts. It assumes the employee has agreed to reduce the standard gap between shifts to 10 hours (clause 7.3).

The calculator assumes that part-time employees have agreed to work above their contracted hours as flex-up hours. It treats these hours as ordinary hours until the employee exceeds 38 hours in a week (clause 8.4).
When shiftworker is selected, the calculator assumes the employee was hired as a shiftworker and is rostered solely for shiftwork during the week. It treats all entered shifts as shiftwork shifts.
The entered start and finish times, unpaid breaks and public-holiday selections accurately reflect the employee’s roster and payroll records.
Any manual ordinary-time or overtime selection applies to the whole entered shift. The user must ensure that the selected classification is appropriate.
limitations: All calculations occur over a fortnight. Calculations that require a longer time period are not included, including regularly worked Sunday rules. The calculator applies a 76-hour full-time threshold and a maximum of 10 worked days; four-week roster requirements must be checked separately against the employee’s roster.
The calculator treats the first entered shift above 9 ordinary hours in a week as the permitted shift of up to 11 ordinary hours. The user must confirm that this is the employee’s rostered long day.
The calculator treats part-time hours above contracted hours as agreed flex-up hours. The user must manually classify any hours that were not validly accepted as flex-up as overtime (clause 8.4).

The calculator treats hours outside the ordinary span as overtime. If the employee has agreed to work those hours under a different arrangement, the user must apply the appropriate manual classification (clause 6.1(b)).

For an insufficient break, the calculator adds an amount equal to 100% of the base hourly rate to the affected hours. The Agreement describes the entitlement as double the rate the employee would otherwise receive. The result must therefore be reviewed if another penalty or loading would otherwise apply (clause 7.3).

For day workers, the calculator deducts the unpaid break duration entered for each shift. Default day-worker shifts start with a 30-minute unpaid break. Shiftworker shifts start with no break deduction because meal and rest breaks for shiftworkers are paid; do not enter paid shiftworker breaks as unpaid breaks (clause 11.5).
The user selects public holidays and must confirm the applicable date, location, substitution arrangements and shift-start treatment against the employee’s records and the Agreement.
exclusion_intro: The calculator only applies the configured rules shown under ‘Show ruleset’ and described above.
Specific areas which are not covered include:

exclusion_groups.title: Specific exclusions
items: The calculator only reviews one pay period. It does not apply longer-period rules, including the 144-hour part-time and 152-hour full-time limits, 19-day and 20-day roster arrangements, 16-day four-day-week arrangement, 9.5-hour four-day-week limit, consecutive-day rules, consecutive days off and regularly-worked-Sunday arrangements.
The calculator treats all shiftworkers the same. It does not apply the special early-morning and night-shift rates for baking-production employees.
The calculator uses adult rates. It does not cover junior, apprentice, trainee, school-based apprentice or supported-wage rates.

exclusion_groups.title: Other items not included
items: Classification progression, higher duties, future wage changes and minimum-wage compliance.
Meal-break compliance and payments, allowances, reimbursements, uniforms, meals, travel, vehicle use and other expenses, apart from the entered break deduction described above.
Recall payments, time off instead of overtime and minimum-payment rules not expressly configured.
Leave, leave loading, superannuation, tax, deductions, termination payments, interest and back-pay calculations.
Approval undertakings, saved provisions, annualised salaries, individual arrangements, employment-contract terms and other arrangements that alter the Agreement’s operation.

closing_paragraphs: These assumptions, limitations and exclusions must be checked against the employee’s actual employment arrangements, roster and payroll records.

coles_2024.title: Scope and assumptions
paragraphs: This calculator provides a guide to selected payments for adult employees under the Coles Retail Enterprise Agreement 2024. It applies the configured ordinary-hour spans, casual loading, minimum paid engagements for part-time and casual employees, weekday and weekend penalties, public-holiday rates, daily and period overtime thresholds, two-tier Monday-to-Saturday overtime rates, generic shiftwork rates and the configured break-between-work-periods rule.
assumptions: The selected instrument, classification, employment type, worker type, base hourly rate and entered shift details are correct, and the employee is a wages-paid team member covered by the Coles Retail Enterprise Agreement 2024.

All calculations are based on one two-week pay period. The calculator assesses full-time ordinary hours against 76 hours for the pay period. Part-time and casual period thresholds are assessed weekly.

The calculator applies an insufficient-break payment when the employee has less than 12 hours between work periods. It assumes the standard 12-hour gap applies and the employee has not selected the 10-hour Roster Choice.
Unless manually marked as overtime, the calculator assumes that any part-time hours above the agreed pattern have been validly varied under the Agreement.

When shiftworker is selected, the calculator assumes the employee is employed as a shiftworker and every entered shift qualifies for the selected shiftwork treatment. It also assumes the employee is not rostered for both shiftwork and non-shiftwork in the same week.
Entered start and finish times, unpaid breaks, public-holiday selections and any manual ordinary-time or overtime selections accurately reflect the employee’s records and applicable arrangements.
Any manual ordinary-time or overtime selection applies to the whole entered shift. The user must ensure that the selected classification is appropriate.
limitations: All calculations occur over a fortnight. Calculations that require a longer time period are not included, including regularly worked Sunday rules. The calculator approximates the fortnightly rules using a 76-hour full-time threshold and a maximum of 10 worked days; the complete four-week roster tests and exact 5-day and 6-day/4-day pattern must be checked separately against the roster.
The calculator treats the first entered shift exceeding 9 ordinary hours in a week as the permitted shift of up to 11 ordinary hours. The user must confirm that this is the rostered long day.

The calculator only partially accounts for part-time overtime outside the agreed or validly varied pattern. It applies weekly and daily thresholds, but the user must manually mark any other hours outside the pattern as overtime.

The calculator classifies work outside the ordinary span as overtime by default. Clause 4.9.5 may allow this work to count as ordinary hours while retaining the applicable overtime rate. The result must be reviewed because a manual ordinary-time selection changes both the classification and payment treatment.
The break-between-work-periods calculation uses the standard 12-hour threshold. If the employee has selected the 10-hour Roster Choice, the result must be reviewed separately.

For day workers, the calculator deducts the unpaid break duration entered for each shift. Default day-worker shifts start with a 30-minute unpaid break. Shiftworker shifts start with no break deduction because meal and rest breaks for shiftworkers are paid; do not enter paid shiftworker breaks as unpaid breaks.
The user selects public holidays and must confirm the applicable date, location, store-level substitution arrangements and shift-start treatment under the Agreement.
exclusion_intro: The calculator only applies the configured rules shown under ‘Show ruleset’ and described above.
Specific areas which are not covered include:
exclusions: Voluntary Additional Shifts, including consent requirements, separate minimum engagements, break treatment and recall treatment.
The 152-hour and 19-day or agreed 20-day four-week roster tests, maximum consecutive days, consecutive days off and regularly-worked-Sunday arrangements.
Baking-production shiftworker provisions and employee-specific saved provisions.
Junior and other special wage rates, classification progression, higher duties, future wage changes and minimum-wage compliance.
Meal-break compliance and payments, allowances, reimbursements, uniforms, meals, travel, vehicle use and other expenses, apart from the entered break deduction described above.
Recall payments, time off instead of overtime and minimum-payment rules not expressly configured.
Leave, leave loading, superannuation, tax, deductions, termination payments, interest and back-pay calculations.
Approval undertakings, saved provisions, annualised salaries, individual arrangements, employment-contract terms and other arrangements that alter the Agreement’s operation.
closing_paragraphs: These assumptions, limitations and exclusions must be checked against the employee’s actual employment arrangements, roster and payroll records.

gria_2026.title: Scope and assumptions
paragraphs: This calculator provides a guide to selected payments for adult employees under the General Retail Industry Award 2020. It applies the configured ordinary-hour spans, casual loading, casual minimum paid engagement, weekday and weekend penalties, public-holiday rates, daily and period overtime thresholds, two-tier Monday-to-Saturday overtime rates, generic shiftwork rates and the configured break-between-work-periods rule.
assumptions: The selected instrument, classification, employment type, worker type, base hourly rate and entered shift details are correct, and the employee is covered by the General Retail Industry Award 2020 without an enterprise agreement or other overriding arrangement.

All calculations are based on one two-week pay period. The calculator assesses full-time ordinary hours against 76 hours for the pay period. Part-time and casual period thresholds are assessed weekly.
The retailer’s trading hours satisfy clause 15.2(c), so the configured ordinary-hour span extends to 11:00 pm on every day.
Unless manually marked as overtime, the calculator assumes that any part-time hours above guaranteed hours are covered by a valid variation to the employee’s guaranteed-hours arrangement.

When shiftworker is selected, the calculator assumes the employee is specifically employed to perform shiftwork and every entered shift qualifies for the selected shiftwork treatment. It also assumes the employee is not rostered for both shiftwork and non-shiftwork in the same week.

The calculator applies an insufficient-break payment when the employee has less than 12 hours between work periods. It assumes the standard 12-hour gap applies and no agreement reducing it to 10 hours is in place.
Entered start and finish times, unpaid breaks, public-holiday selections and any manual ordinary-time or overtime selections accurately reflect the employee’s records and applicable arrangements.
Any manual ordinary-time or overtime selection applies to the whole entered shift. The user must ensure that the selected classification is appropriate.
limitations: All calculations occur over a fortnight. Calculations that require a longer time period are not included, including regularly worked Sunday rules. The calculator approximates the fortnightly rules using a 76-hour full-time threshold and a maximum of 10 worked days; other averaging arrangements and the Award’s exact weekly and four-week roster tests must be checked separately against the roster.
The calculator treats the first entered shift exceeding 9 ordinary hours in a week as the permitted shift of up to 11 ordinary hours. The user must confirm that this is the rostered long day.
The configured 11:00 pm span assumes the retailer satisfies clause 15.2(c). If the retailer has different trading hours, the applicable ordinary-hour span must be checked separately.

The calculator only partially accounts for part-time overtime outside guaranteed hours or a valid variation. It applies weekly and daily thresholds, but the user must manually mark any other hours outside the arrangement as overtime.
Shiftworker mode applies the weekday shiftwork loading to all submitted Monday-to-Friday hours. The user confirms that the employee and each entered shift satisfy the Award’s shiftwork definitions.
The break-between-work-periods calculation uses the standard 12-hour threshold. An agreed reduction to 10 hours requires separate review.

For day workers, the calculator deducts the unpaid break duration entered for each shift. Default day-worker shifts start with a 30-minute unpaid break. Shiftworker shifts start with no break deduction because meal and rest breaks for shiftworkers are paid; do not enter paid shiftworker breaks as unpaid breaks.
The user selects public holidays and must confirm the applicable date, location and substitution arrangements.
exclusion_intro: The calculator only applies the configured rules shown under ‘Show ruleset’ and described above.
Specific areas which are not covered include:
exclusions: The 1.5-hour minimum engagement for qualifying full-time secondary-school-student casuals.
Baking-production shiftworker provisions and the special newsagency and video-shop ordinary-hour spans.
Three-week, four-week and longer full-time averaging arrangements, the 19-day four-week limit and associated rostered-day-off arrangements.
Junior, apprentice, trainee, school-based apprentice and supported-wage rates.
Classification progression, higher duties, future annual wage changes and minimum-wage compliance.
Meal-break compliance and payments, allowances, reimbursements, uniforms, meals, travel, vehicle use and other expenses, apart from the entered break deduction described above.
Recall payments, time off instead of overtime and minimum-payment rules not expressly configured.
Leave, leave loading, superannuation, tax, deductions, termination payments, interest and back-pay calculations.
Enterprise agreements, annualised salaries, individual flexibility arrangements, employment-contract terms and other arrangements that may apply instead of or alongside the Award.
closing_paragraphs: These assumptions, limitations and exclusions must be checked against the employee’s actual employment arrangements, roster and payroll records.
